Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We chatted internally this morning about next steps for a Dedicated (reserved) GPU pool for HoloHealth. Before we lock a scope and SOW, two quick confirmations would help us size things correctly:

- Preferred primary region for the pool (region where low latency is most important). You mentioned EU during the demo — can you confirm Ireland (eu-west-1) specifically?
- Expected steady-state concurrency / qps and any launch day traffic multipliers (e.g., 2x baseline for marketing launch).
- Any strict compliance constraints (SOC2 / data residency) that require private deployment vs hosted dedicated?

If you can share answers and any internal network contacts, Monica and I will produce a short implementation plan (network checklist, autoscale + warm-burst policy recommendation, tentative kickoff date). I attached a one-page SOW stub for reference.

Jasmine

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks — yes, Ireland (eu-west-1) is our preference for primary capacity due to our EU customer base and data residency rules. We have two product spikes a quarter where traffic can hit ~3x baseline for a 48–72h window; typical steady-state is ~250 concurrent requests.

Compliance: SOC2 is a hard requirement. We will need audit log exports and access to KMS integration. Private deployment (VPC peering) is preferable but we're open to a hosted-dedicated model if the audit and residency guarantees are documented in the SOW.

Network: cc'ing our ops lead A. Lee (alee@holohealth.com) — they will provide IP ranges and peering contacts.

We reviewed the SOW stub and have a few procurement questions (billing terms / early-termination). Will get back with those, but for planning please proceed with Ireland as primary and a standby pool in us-west-2 as a failover.

Best,
Priya

Thanks Priya — copying internal implementation and ops.

High level recommendation (based on your inputs):
- Primary pool: eu-west-1 (Ireland), capacity sized for 250 concurrent steady-state.
- Warm pool / autoscale: min nodes sized for baseline (250) with a warm standby of ~25% capacity to keep KV caches warm.
- Burst policy: allow automatic scale up to 3x baseline for up to 72 hours; we recommend a soft cap policy that ramps to full burst over 15 minutes to avoid noisy neighbor impacts.
- Standby pool: us-west-2 for DR/failover — traffic will route by policy (latency + residency).
- Compliance: we'll include SOC2 evidence delivery (audit logs, S3 export cadence) in SOW; KMS integration is supported (bring-your-own-key).

Attached: implementation checklist (network diagram + quick SOW draft). Next internal step: Prioyom will propose the sprint and resource owners; Karthik will outline the netops checklist (BGP, peering, firewall rules).

Can we lock a kickoff on Tuesday June 22 at 10:00 AM UTC? That gives us a week to finalize SOW and procure approvals.

Monica
